log.text: Light Screen up on P2's side

decisions.rationale: Lead Sneasler and Mamoswine apply immediate pressure to Gengar, Tyranitar, and Excadrill with Fake Out, Close Combat, and Ground/Ice attacks. Armarouge provides Wide Guard against Rock Slide and Make It Rain while threatening Steel targets, and Farigiraf supplies Trick Room, Helping Hand, and priority denial for the sand matchup.
decisions.notebook: Prioritize disrupting the opponent’s Sand Rush mode and spread attacks. Preserve Armarouge as the Wide Guard pivot and use Farigiraf’s Trick Room option when sand-boosted speed becomes decisive.

decisions.rationale: Grimmsnarl+Excadrill lead exploits the TR matchup: Grimmsnarl is immune to Farigiraf PsychicNoise (Dark typing) and sets Reflect via Prankster (unaffected by Armor Tail since it's ally-side). Under TR, Excadrill (140 Spe) outspeeds Sneasler (154-189) and guarantees OHKO with High Horsepower (2x SE, 105.9-210.3%). Sneasler's Close Combat OHKOs Excadrill but Focus Sash saves it. Grimmsnarl also walls Armarouge (immune to Psychic, resists Fire) and Archaludon (resists Dragon/Steel). Gengar-Mega in back provides Shadow Tag trapping, 200 Speed, and Taunt to prevent future TR. Tyranitar provides sand (Excadrill to 280 Spe), Crunch (2x SE on Farigiraf), Rock Slide (2x SE on Armarouge), and hard-walls Armarouge Armor Cannon (NVE 0.5x, only 13.5-19.8%).
decisions.notebook: Key damage benchmarks: Excadrill High Horsepower→Sneasler guaranteed OHKO (105.9-210.3%); Sneasler Close Combat→Tyranitar guaranteed OHKO (164.3-237.7%); Sneasler Close Combat→Excadrill guaranteed OHKO but Focus Sash saves (163.6-234.2%); Armarouge Armor Cannon→Gholdengo guaranteed OHKO (133-190.9%); Armarouge Armor Cannon→Tyranitar only 13.5-19.8% (NVE 0.5x); Farigiraf PsychicNoise→Gengar possible OHKO (93.4-137.2%); Gengar Shadow Ball→Armarouge possible OHKO (65.6-123.8%); Excadrill High Horsepower→Armarouge possible OHKO (76-136.3%); Tyranitar Crunch→Farigiraf 51.1-95.4% (2x SE); Grimmsnarl Spirit Break→Farigiraf 21.6-40.5% + SpA -1. Sneasler has Poison Touch (not Unburden) with Black Belt (no consumable). Farigiraf Mental Herb cures Taunt turn 1. Armor Tail blocks opposing priority targeting Farigiraf's side but NOT ally-side screens, self-Protect, or same-team Fake Out. Under TR Excadrill (140) outspeeds Sneasler (154-189). Grimmsnarl immune to Psychic (Dark). Gengar-Mega walls Sneasler (immune Fighting, resists Poison). Game 1 lead: Grimmsnarl+Excadrill, back Gengar+Tyranitar. Plan: tank TR turn 1 with Reflect, Excadrill OHKOs Sneasler under TR turn 2, Grimmsnarl Spirit Breaks Farigiraf, then bring Gengar-Mega+Tyranitar for cleanup with Shadow Tag, sand, and Taunt.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out stops Grimmsnarl from establishing screens while High Horsepower pressures Excadrill through its Ground weakness, forcing its Focus Sash and disrupting the Sand Rush mode before pivoting to Wide Guard or Trick Room options.
decisions.notebook: Prioritize disrupting Sand Rush and spread attacks; preserve Armarouge as the Wide Guard pivot and Farigiraf as the Trick Room option when sand speed becomes decisive.

decisions.rationale: Grimmsnarl Reflect + Excadrill Protect. Sneasler will likely Fake Out Excadrill to prevent the OHKO — Protect blocks it, and Grimmsnarl's Prankster Reflect (+1 priority) goes up before Mamoswine's attacks. If Sneasler instead Fake Outs Grimmsnarl, it flinches (no Reflect) but both stay at full HP and Sneasler burns its only Fake Out window. Either way, turn 2 Excadrill freely OHKOs Sneasler with High Horsepower, and I can set Reflect then if needed. This minimizes risk while guaranteeing Excadrill's Sash stays intact and Sneasler's Fake Out is spent.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lead: Grimmsnarl+Excadrill vs Sneasler+Mamoswine. Turn 1 plan: Reflect+Protect to burn Sneasler Fake Out and set screens. Turn 2: Excadrill High Horsepower OHKOs Sneasler (guaranteed 105.9-210.3%), Grimmsnarl follows up. Back: Gengar+Tyranitar for Shadow Tag+sand cleanup. Key benchmarks: Excadrill HH→Sneasler OHKO; Sneasler CC→Excadrill OHKO but Sash saves; Sneasler CC→Tyranitar OHKO (164.3-237.7%). Gengar-Mega walls Sneasler (immune Fighting, resists Poison). Farigiraf Mental Herb cures Taunt turn 1; Armor Tail blocks opposing priority on Farigiraf's side. Under TR Excadrill (140) outspeeds Sneasler (154-189). Grimmsnarl immune to Psychic (Dark). Prankster Reflect/Light Screen at +1 priority; Dark-types immune to Prankster status moves.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler moves first and Close Combat removes Excadrill's Focus Sash; Mamoswine's priority Ice Shard then reliably finishes the 1 HP Excadrill while avoiding High Horsepower's accuracy risk, eliminating the Sand Rush and spread-attack threat.
decisions.notebook: Prioritize disrupting Sand Rush and spread attacks. Preserve Armarouge as the Wide Guard pivot and Farigiraf as the Trick Room option when sand speed becomes decisive.

decisions.rationale: Grimmsnarl Reflect (Prankster +1) goes up before Sneasler's attacks, providing 8-turn physical damage reduction for the team. Excadrill High Horsepower guarantees the OHKO on Sneasler (105.9-210.3%, no Sash). Even if the opponent doubles into Excadrill, Sash saves from Sneasler's hit, Excadrill KOs Sneasler, and I trade Excadrill for the opponent's most dangerous Pokemon while keeping Reflect active. Switching to Gengar is too risky — Mamoswine HH OHKOs Gengar-Mega (2x SE Ground vs Poison, 148.9-211.7%). Spirit Break on Sneasler is only neutral (28.9-56.8%) and doesn't remove the threat.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lead: Grimmsnarl+Excadrill vs Sneasler+Mamoswine. Turn 1: Grimmsnarl flinched (no Reflect), Excadrill Protected (blocked Mamoswine HH). Turn 2 plan: Reflect+HH→Sneasler for guaranteed KO. Key benchmarks: Excadrill HH→Sneasler OHKO (105.9-210.3%); Sneasler CC→Excadrill OHKO but Sash saves; Mamoswine HH→Gengar-Mega OHKO (148.9-211.7%, 2x SE Ground vs Poison) — do NOT switch Gengar into Mamoswine; Sneasler Dire Claw→Grimmsnarl 57.4-84.2% (survives from 87%); Spirit Break→Sneasler only neutral 28.9-56.8% (Fairy 2x Fighting × 0.5x Poison = 1x). Sneasler (154-189) outspeeds Excadrill (140) but Grimmsnarl Reflect at Prankster +1 goes first. Back: Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag + Tyranitar sand for cleanup. Gengar-Mega walls Sneasler (immune Fighting, resists Poison) but must avoid Mamoswine HH. Farigiraf Mental Herb cures Taunt; Armor Tail blocks opposing priority on Farigiraf's side.

decisions.rationale: Send in Gengar, not Tyranitar. Sneasler Close Combat vs Tyranitar is a guaranteed OHKO (109.7-158.5% through Reflect) — Tyranitar is a pure sack with zero upside. Mamoswine HH vs Gengar through Reflect is 99.3-140.9% — not a guaranteed OHKO, giving Gengar a real survival chance. If Gengar lives, it Mega Evolves next turn for Shadow Tag (game-changing). If it faints, we still have Grimmsnarl+Tyranitar at 2v4 (playable). The Tyranitar route leads to 2v4, then Gengar faces the same HH threat later, risking 1v4 collapse. Sneasler also cannot meaningfully damage Gengar (Fighting immune, Poison resisted), so only Mamoswine threatens it.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag is the primary win condition. Mamoswine HH vs non-Mega Gengar through Reflect: 99.3-140.9% (possible OHKO, ~25% survival). Sneasler Close Combat vs Tyranitar: 109.7-158.5% GUARANTEED OHKO even through Reflect — never send Tyranitar into Sneasler. Sneasler Dire Claw vs Grimmsnarl through Reflect (Sneasler -1 Def/SpD): 38.1-55.9% (survives from 87%). Sneasler cannot hurt Gengar-Mega (Fighting immune, Poison 0.5x). Opponent gets one free switch before Shadow Tag; watch for Archaludon Snarl (Dark 2x vs Ghost). Plan: Gengar in now, Mega Evolve next turn for Shadow Tag, break Mamoswine Focus Sash with Shadow Ball, Grimmsnarl supports with screens/Protect. Tyranitar reserved for after Sneasler is eliminated or as late-game sand sack.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler should pressure Grimmsnarl with super-effective Dire Claw while Mamoswine targets Gengar with High Horsepower, the strongest immediate threat and a possible OHKO. This preserves both active attackers and avoids wasting attacks into immunities.

Mega Evolve Gengar with Protect to safely activate Shadow Tag — Gengar cannot risk High Horsepower (99.3-140.9% through Reflect, ~75% KO). Grimmsnarl Spirit Breaks Mamoswine to break Focus Sash (21.2-38.9%), setting up a clean Shadow Ball KO next turn while both foes are Shadow Tag trapped. Grimmsnarl survives even worst-case double-target (23.3-33.7% + 38.1-55.9% = 61.4-89.6% from 87% HP). If Mamoswine Protects, it wastes its turn and remains trapped. Sneasler is completely helpless vs Gengar-Mega (Fighting immune, Poison 0.25x).
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag is primary win con. Mamoswine Focus Sash must be broken before KO. Gengar Shadow Ball vs Mamoswine: 34.6-66.5%. Grimmsnarl Spirit Break vs Mamoswine: 21.2-38.9%. Mamoswine HH vs Grimmsnarl through Reflect: 23.3-33.7%. Sneasler Dire Claw vs Grimmsnarl through Reflect (-1 Def): 38.1-55.9%. Sneasler cannot damage Gengar-Mega meaningfully (Fighting 0x, Poison 0.25x). Sneasler Close Combat vs Tyranitar: guaranteed OHKO even through Reflect — never send Tyranitar into Sneasler. Tyranitar reserved as late-game sand sack or after Sneasler eliminated. Watch for Archaludon Snarl (Dark 2x vs Ghost) and Armarouge Wide Guard. Opponent gets one free switch before Shadow Tag locks in (switches resolve pre-Mega).

decisions.rationale: Dire Claw guarantees the KO on Grimmsnarl, removing Prankster and Reflect support. High Horsepower then pressures Gengar-Mega for a possible knockout while preserving the chance to win the active exchange despite Gengar moving first.
Keep Sneasler active to threaten the weakened Grimmsnarl, while switching Mamoswine's slot to Farigiraf, which is immune to Gengar's Shadow Ball and preserves the Trick Room option.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Armarouge for Wide Guard; use Farigiraf as the Trick Room option if opposing sand or spread pressure makes conventional Speed unfavorable.

decisions.rationale: Grimmsnarl must Protect — Sneasler's Dire Claw is a guaranteed KO from 35% HP and Sneasler outspeeds, so Grimmsnarl cannot act before fainting. Switching to Tyranitar is fatal (Close Combat guaranteed OHKO). Gengar Shadow Balls Mamoswine: KOing Mamoswine removes the only threat to Gengar (HH 78.8-113.9% possible OHKO), and if Mamoswine falls, Sneasler is trapped by Shadow Tag and cannot damage Gengar at all — near-guaranteed win. Targeting Sneasler instead still leaves Mamoswine free to OHKO Gengar this turn, making Mamoswine the priority elimination target.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag is primary win con. Both foes trapped — no switches available for opponent. Sneasler cannot damage Gengar-Mega (Fighting 0x, Poison 0.25x, Normal 0x). Mamoswine HH vs Gengar: 78.8-113.9% possible OHKO — Mamoswine is priority elimination target. Gengar Shadow Ball vs Mamoswine: 41.5-80% (possible KO from 64%). Gengar Shadow Ball vs Sneasler (-1 SpD): 61-116.1% possible OHKO. Sneasler Dire Claw guaranteed KO on Grimmsnarl from 35%. Sneasler Close Combat guaranteed OHKO on Tyranitar even through Reflect — never bring Tyranitar into Sneasler. Tyranitar reserved as late-game sand sack only after Sneasler eliminated. Watch for Archaludon Snarl (Dark 2x vs Ghost) and Armarouge Wide Guard from unrevealed foe Pokémon.

decisions.rationale: Dire Claw reliably KOs Grimmsnarl from 35%, while Helping Hand boosts Sneasler before it attacks and Farigiraf remains immune to Gengar's Shadow Ball.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Armarouge for Wide Guard; use Farigiraf as the Trick Room option when opposing sand or spread pressure makes conventional Speed unfavorable.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Gengar-Mega)
decisions.rationale: Grimmsnarl uses Light Screen (Prankster priority, guaranteed before damage) to halve Farigiraf's Psychic Noise from possible OHKO range (78.8-115.3%) to survivable 39-58%. Gengar Shadow Balls Sneasler at -1 SpD for a possible OHKO (61-116.1%); if Sneasler faints, it cannot Dire Claw Grimmsnarl, so Grimmsnarl survives at 35% and can Spirit Break Farigiraf next turn (21.6-40.5% + SpA drop) alongside Gengar Sludge Bomb (41-75.9%) for a combined 62.6-116.4% double-target KO on Farigiraf. If Sneasler survives, it still cannot damage Gengar at all, and Gengar outspeeds Farigiraf to Taunt it next turn before any Trick Room. Shadow Tag keeps both foes trapped regardless.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag traps both foes — no switches for opponent. Sneasler cannot damage Gengar (Fighting 0x, Poison 0.25x, Normal 0x). Farigiraf Psychic Noise is 2x SE on Gengar: 78.8-115.3% raw, ~39-58% under Light Screen. Gengar Sludge Bomb vs Farigiraf: 41-75.9% (61.5-113.9% with Helping Hand — possible OHKO). Grimmsnarl Spirit Break vs Farigiraf: 21.6-40.5% + -1 SpA. Tyranitar Crunch vs Farigiraf: 51.1-95.4% (2x SE). Sneasler Close Combat OHKOs Tyranitar even through Reflect — never bring Tyranitar into Sneasler. Under TR, Farigiraf (80-112) and Sneasler (154-189) outspeed Gengar (200); without TR, Gengar outspeeds both and can KO Farigiraf before it moves. Key win con: eliminate Farigiraf to remove the only Psychic Noise threat to Gengar; Sneasler is then helpless. Watch for 4th foe: Archaludon Snarl (Dark 2x vs Ghost), Armarouge Expanding Force (Psychic 2x), Dedenne Eerie Impulse (SpA -2).

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

selection: Trick Room (all adjacent, including ally Sneasler)
decisions.rationale: Close Combat threatens an immediate 4x knockout on Tyranitar, while Trick Room establishes the speed mode for Armarouge against opposing sand pressure and avoids exposing Farigiraf to an unnecessary attack this turn.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Gengar Shadow Ball KOs Sneasler at 3% before it can Close Combat Tyranitar (Gengar 200 > Sneasler 154-189). Tyranitar Crunch hits Farigiraf for 51.1-95.4% (2x SE). If Sneasler Protects (priority +4), Shadow Ball is wasted but Tyranitar still Crunches Farigiraf; under TR next turn Sneasler Close Combats Tyranitar (OHKO) but Gengar KOs Sneasler and Tyranitar finishes Farigiraf with a second Crunch (102-190.8% combined = guaranteed KO). Both active foes are eliminated in every scenario. Taunt on Farigiraf is useless because Mental Herb cures it immediately, so preventing TR isn't possible — but eliminating both foes under TR is the win path. Best case: Sneasler doesn't Protect, Tyranitar survives, both foes fall over two turns. Worst case: Sneasler Protects, Tyranitar falls, but both foes still die and Gengar faces the 4th Pokémon alone at 42-100%.
decisions.notebook: Mental Herb on Farigiraf cures Taunt immediately — never Taunt Farigiraf while Mental Herb is intact. Sneasler Close Combat guaranteed OHKOs Tyranitar through Reflect (109.7-158.5%). Gengar Shadow Ball guaranteed KOs Sneasler at 3% (61-116.1%). Tyranitar Crunch vs Farigiraf: 51.1-95.4% (2x SE Dark vs Normal/Psychic). Gengar Sludge Bomb vs Farigiraf: 41-75.9% (neutral). Combined Crunch+Sludge Bomb: 92.1-171.3% (likely KO but not guaranteed). Under TR, Farigiraf (80-112) and Tyranitar (81) act before Sneasler (154-189) and Gengar (200). Sneasler cannot damage Gengar (Fighting 0x, Poison 0.25x, Normal 0x). Key win con: eliminate Farigiraf to remove Psychic Noise threat; Sneasler is then helpless vs Gengar. Watch for 4th foe: Archaludon Snarl 2x vs Ghost, Armarouge Expanding Force 2x vs Ghost, Dedenne Eerie Impulse SpA-2. Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag traps all foes — no switches for opponent while Gengar is active.

decisions.rationale: Farigiraf acts before Gengar under Trick Room. Psychic Noise damages Gengar first, then Helping-Hand-free Armor Cannon provides enough combined damage to guarantee the KO from 94% across the shown ranges, removing the immediate Shadow Ball threat while preserving Wide Guard for later spread pressure.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Armarouge as the primary Wide Guard user against opposing spread attacks. Farigiraf is the preferred Trick Room option when opposing sand or spread pressure makes conventional Speed unfavorable.

decisions.rationale: Under TR, Armarouge moves before Gengar and Farigiraf's Helping Hand (priority +5) can boost Expanding Force to potentially KO Gengar (91.2-132.1%). Tyranitar Crunch guarantees KO on 17% Farigiraf (51.1-95.4% vs 17% HP). Gengar Protect (priority +4) blocks Armarouge's boosted Expanding Force regardless of Farigiraf's action. If Farigiraf doesn't Protect, it dies and next turn is 2v1 vs trapped Armarouge (Shadow Tag) for the game. If Farigiraf Protects, Gengar stays safe and Farigiraf drops to ~10% from sandstorm chip — repeat next turn. Protecting Gengar is critical: losing it means losing Shadow Tag and the opponent can bring a 4th Pokémon.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Mamoswine/Sneasler/Armarouge/Farigiraf — Archaludon and Dedenne NOT brought. If we win Game 1, opponent must bring different team for Game 2. Farigiraf Mental Herb still intact (never been Taunted). Armarouge Quiet nature = min Speed investment, under TR moves before Gengar but after Tyranitar. Armarouge Flash Fire — don't use Fire moves into it. Key win con: preserve Gengar-Mega (Shadow Tag traps all foes, no switches while active). Under TR, Gengar (200 Spe) moves last — always Protect Gengar when threatened by boosted SE Psychic moves. Tyranitar Crunch 2x SE vs both Armarouge (Fire/Psychic) and Farigiraf (Normal/Psychic). Reflect expires in 3 turns, Light Screen in 6. For Game 2 prep: opponent likely adjusts team composition; watch for Archaludon Snarl (2x vs Ghost) and Dedenne Eerie Impulse (SpA-2) as Gengar counters.

decisions.rationale: Under Trick Room, Armarouge acts before Gengar. Expanding Force is the only listed attack with a realistic chance to KO Gengar before it can retaliate; Tyranitar is immune to it, while Armor Cannon cannot reliably finish Gengar. Farigiraf has no available action.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Armarouge as the primary Wide Guard user against opposing spread attacks. Farigiraf is the preferred Trick Room setter when opposing sand or spread pressure makes conventional Speed unfavorable.

decisions.rationale: 2v1 endgame: only Armarouge (93%) remains. Under TR, Tyranitar (81 Spe) moves first and Crunches for 47.9-87.5%, dropping Armarouge to 5.5-45.1%. Gengar's Shadow Ball (79.2-150%) then easily finishes. If Armarouge Protects, both whiff but I keep dominant 2v1 with 2 TR turns left. If Armarouge attacks Gengar with Expanding Force (61.3-88.3%, possible KO), Gengar may fall but Armarouge is already weakened — Tyranitar KOs next turn since Expanding Force is 0x into Tyranitar (Dark) and Armor Cannon is 0.5x NVE + Light Screen. No losing scenario exists.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Mamoswine/Sneasler/Armarouge/Farigiraf — Archaludon and Dedenne NOT brought. Farigiraf fainted (Mental Herb used on TR turn). Armarouge Quiet nature, Flash Fire, Charcoal — only Fire/Psychic moves; Expanding Force 0x into Tyranitar (Dark), Armor Cannon 0.5x NVE into Tyranitar (Rock). Key: Tyranitar Crunch 2x SE vs Armarouge; Gengar Shadow Ball 2x SE vs Armarouge. Under TR, Tyranitar outspeeds Armarouge (81 < 85-114 reversed). After TR expires, Armarouge outspeeds Tyranitar but can't meaningfully damage it. For Game 2 prep: opponent must bring different team (6-mon roster, lost Game 1). Watch for Archaludon Snarl (2x vs Ghost) and Dedenne Eerie Impulse (SpA-2) as Gengar counters. Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag traps — no switches while active.

reflections.summary: The game was lost mainly because Trick Room was established too late: Mamoswine and Sneasler were removed before Farigiraf could support Armarouge, while attacks were spent into Mega Gengar's Protect and the opponent's screens and sand compounded the disadvantage. The four brought were strategically workable—Sneasler and Mamoswine supplied immediate pressure, while Farigiraf and Armarouge fit the Trick Room plan—but the sequencing did not let that plan function. No Mega Stone holder was brought or evolved on your side; Armarouge was still the appropriate slow-mode attacker, but it needed earlier Trick Room support.
reflections.adjustment: Lead Sneasler with Farigiraf and use Fake Out to deny the opposing setup or Mega Gengar while setting Trick Room immediately. After Trick Room is active, avoid committing attacks into Gengar's Protect; use Armarouge's Wide Guard or Protect when appropriate and redirect pressure toward Tyranitar or the non-protected target.
reflections.notebook: Opponent combines Mega Gengar Protect and strong Shadow Ball pressure with Grimmsnarl dual screens and Tyranitar sand, while Excadrill can use Focus Sash and Protect to buy turns. Expect defensive Protect cycles around Gengar and prioritize establishing Trick Room before sacrificing the fast attackers. Preserve Armarouge as the primary Wide Guard user against opposing spread attacks; Farigiraf remains the preferred Trick Room setter when opposing sand or spread pressure makes conventional Speed unfavorable. Future plan: pair Farigiraf with Sneasler's Fake Out support to establish Trick Room early, then avoid wasting attacks into Gengar's Protect.

reflections.summary: Won through Gengar-Mega Shadow Ball cleaning up weakened Mamoswine and Sneasler, then Tyranitar Crunch (2x SE) finishing Farigiraf and Armarouge. Opponent's Trick Room backfired: under TR, slow Tyranitar outsped and KO'd Armarouge before it could act. Screens from Grimmsnarl and well-timed Protects minimized damage during setup. No decision errors recorded.
reflections.adjustment: Excadrill fell early to Sneasler Close Combat + Mamoswine Ice Shard after only absorbing one Protect. Consider leading Tyranitar alongside Grimmsnarl to threaten Sneasler with Rock Slide and discourage Fake Out, preserving Excadrill for Sand Rush cleanup if Trick Room appears again.
reflections.notebook: Opponent 6-mon roster: Mamoswine (FocusSash/ThickFat/Jolly), Sneasler (BlackBelt/PoisonTouch/Jolly — Fake Out, Close Combat, Dire Claw, Upper Hand), Armarouge (Charcoal/FlashFire/Quiet — Armor Cannon, Expanding Force, Wide Guard, Protect), Farigiraf (MentalHerb/ArmorTail/Modest — TR, Helping Hand, Psychic Noise, Protect), Archaludon (Leftovers/Stamina/Modest — Dragon Pulse, Flash Cannon, Snarl, Protect), Dedenne (WacanBerry/CheekPouch/Timid — Nuzzle, Helping Hand, Eerie Impulse, Protect). Game 1 brought: Mamoswine/Sneasler/Armarouge/Farigiraf; Archaludon and Dedenne NOT brought. Farigiraf Mental Herb consumed on TR turn. Armarouge only Fire/Psychic attacking moves — 0x into Tyranitar (Dark) with Expanding Force, 0.5x NVE Armor Cannon into Tyranitar (Rock). Under TR, Tyranitar (81 Spe) outspeeds Armarouge (Quiet). Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag traps — no switches while active. Archaludon Snarl (2x vs Ghost) and Dedenne Eerie Impulse (SpA-2) are Gengar counters; expect one or both in Game 2. Opponent lost Game 1 and may adjust leads or bring Archaludon/Dedenne. Plan: keep Tyranitar for Armarouge/Farigiraf matchup; preserve Excadrill better; Gengar-Mega Shadow Ball is primary Armarouge answer.
